### ① Derived judgments

1. File surface. One commit (dceca372, author Claude, PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head repo = base repo, draft, base `main`, trailers `Claude-Session:` + `Co-authored-by: Claude`, no model identifier). `git diff --numstat 6f094645 dceca372`, the REST file listing (+29 / −31, 4 files) and the PR body agree on exactly four paths: `rules/field-types.md` +1/−15 (264 → 250 lines), `rules/relationships.md` +8/−15 (420 → 413), `evals/objects-fields-relationships.json` +19/−0 (101 → 120), `evals/README.md` +1/−1 (12 lines both). The claim (6595137045) named the two rule files, "plus their evals where the edited lines are covered"; the fixture is that, and the README is the fixture's one-line index, so it rides with it. Nothing outside `skills/objectstack-data/` is touched; the ratchet script is not in the diff. Correct, and on surface.
2. The code the new text asserts, read on the head. `statesDeleteSemantics` (engine.ts L1859–1865) admits `master_detail`, `lookup` and `tree` unconditionally and a `user` field only when `deleteBehavior` is one of `set_null` / `cascade` / `restrict` (L1848). `cascadeRelationBehavior` (L19713–19714) resolves a non-`master_detail` field to `fdef.deleteBehavior || 'set_null'`, and the docblock at L19705–19707 says the fallback is never what a `user` gets. `field.zod.ts` L3339–3340 materializes `set_null` on `lookup` and `tree` only; a bare `user` field parses with no key (pinned by the test's first case, L197–201). The user-field test pins: undeclared → holder kept with the id unchanged (L203–218, four shapes including `required: true`); `restrict` → `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` with the same code and status a `lookup` restrict answers (L221–255); `cascade` → the rows holding the user are deleted, a bystander stays, and a later `restrict` rolls the cascade back as one unit of work (L281–316); `set_null` single → field `null`, multi → only the member removed and an emptied set is `[]` (L319–346); `set_null` on a required single-valued field → refused (L348–359). So the field-types `user` row ("no default — declared, deleting the user acts as on `lookup`: `cascade` deletes the holders, `set_null` clears the field or drops that member, `restrict` refuses with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`; undeclared, the field keeps the deleted user's id") states exactly what the code does, and the relationships paragraph's first two sentences ("The walk also reads `lookup` and `tree` (`set_null` by default … or an authored `cascade` / `restrict`), and a `user` field only when it declares a value … undeclared, the field keeps the deleted user's id") do too. The three values that exist, what each does, the join-only-when-declared rule and the `409` code are all correct against the code.
3. The required + `set_null` sentence, relationships.md L179–180: "`restrict`, and `set_null` on a `required` field, refuse the delete with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`." The code escalates unconditionally only for a single-valued field (L20073–20076, `requiredSetNull && !multiValued`). For a `multiple: true` required field the decision is deferred to after the probe (L20167–20175) and refuses only when some row's set would be EMPTIED by the member removal; a row that still holds another live member is written the non-empty remainder and the delete goes through. That is a maintainer ruling (#9688, 2026-08-19), pinned at `engine-cascade-delete.test.ts` L334 ("a required MULTI-VALUE lookup now REMOVES the member when the remainder stays non-empty") and L416–459, and the engine's own comment calls the unconditional reading "broader than the contract". The skill's sentence is the pre-ruling reading, and it reaches `user` fields through the paragraph's own "exactly as a `lookup` does". A `watchers`-shaped field (`multiple: true`, `required: true`, `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'`) is the natural case the paragraph is teaching, and the skill tells its author that deleting any watcher is refused when the engine refuses only the last one. The code contradicts the statement for that case: M1. The fix is a parenthetical; relationships.md has 43 tokens of headroom. `fields.mdx` L309 on main carries the same simplification for the `user` field, so the docs page is not a defence of the sentence and owes its own follow-up (③). Eval 6 is untouched by this: its `owner` is single-valued and its `watchers` is not required.
4. The only difference is the example child name (`invoice_line_item` vs `invoice_line`), not a fact. Nothing taught only there. Survives. Measured 14 lines, 361 bytes, as the body says.

Survives. Measured 14 lines, 534 bytes, plus 79 bytes of ToC (123 → 44) = 613, as the body says.

### ④ Design judgment

Per hits file, against the card's scenario (an AI authoring metadata from the skill must know that `deleteBehavior` on a `user` field is enforced, has no default, and what each value does when the user is deleted) and the code on main:

The `must_not_contain` on `deleteBehavior: 'cascade'` is the right negative: a reader who confuses "block the delete" with "delete the tickets" fails it. Holds; untouched by M1 (`owner` single-valued, `watchers` not required).
- `skills/objectstack-data/evals/README.md`: one index line, the right file. The inserted phrase "a `user` field's included" reads as a fragment (S1). Holds.
